description: WHEN OTHER of 9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST at :858-865, the THIRD and last arm of the three-arm EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :836, whose WHEN order - NORMAL at :837, NOTFND at :839, OTHER at :858 - is preserved exactly (gate G30), and the last of the program's three file-error arms, with ERROR-FILE 'CUSTDAT '. This file also carries the folder's proof of a NEGATIVE, and the negative is the reason it is worth reading twice. app/cbl/COACTVWC.cbl is 941 lines long and contains ZERO occurrences of STARTBR, READNEXT, READPREV, RESETBR and ENDBR - all five counted - and therefore zero occurrences of DFHRESP(ENDFILE) as well. Its only file verbs are the three keyed EXEC CICS READs at :727, :776 and :826. common.FileStatus nonetheless publishes END_OF_FILE = '10' among its unified batch-and-CICS outcome vocabulary, because the eleven batch programs need it, and gate G47 asks that each of those outcomes be exercised per repository call site. The honest answer for THIS program is that '10' has no dedicated arm to reach: there is no browse on which an end-of-file condition is even meaningful, so an end-of-file reported against any of the three keyed reads matches neither WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL) nor WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) and lands in WHEN OTHER, composing the generic file-error message this case pins byte for byte. Asserting that, rather than quietly leaving the outcome undriven, is what stops a later implementer inventing a DFHRESP(ENDFILE) branch the COBOL does not have (practice B5). The corroboration is already in the harness and is not this file's invention: COACTVWCParityTest.forcedSite at :403-411 REFUSES any forced outcome other than OTHER, and refuses END_OF_FILE with the reason 'END_OF_FILE is a browse outcome and COACTVWC opens no browse'. So the mechanism used here is the one the schema and the adapter actually provide, and it is worth naming precisely because ParityCase.ScreenRequest.forcedOutcomes is keyed by RepositoryOperation and all three of this program's reads are READ, so the key alone cannot name a site: the site is named by the one dataset the case declares EMPTY, which is CUSTDAT at 500 bytes over CVCUS01Y, and the rule is enforced at :412-428 where exactly one empty dataset is required - none would leave the outcome forcing nothing, two would leave it ambiguous. Because CCXREF and ACCTDAT still hold their rows, the two reads before the driven one still succeed and the flow still reaches the site being driven. That flow is worth following, because it turns on two guards that can never fire. The main EVALUATE TRUE at :323-383 takes its THIRD arm, WHEN CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :361, since the inbound CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 and the AID is DFHENTER, which the first CSSTRPFY arm resolves to the ENTER token and which the invalid-key remap at :306-314 therefore leaves alone. 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS takes the ELSE at :632 - the typed ACCTSIDI is neither '*' nor spaces - and 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT, whose :650 defensively SETs FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK on entry, passes the blank guard at :653-662 and the not-numeric-or-zeroes guard at :666-676 and reaches its ELSE at :677-680, where :678 moves CC-ACCT-ID into CDEMO-ACCT-ID and :679 SETs FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID, clearing that entry default. So INPUT-ERROR is still false when :364 tests it, the arm takes the ELSE at :368, and 9000-READ-ACCT runs at :369-370 followed by 1000-SEND-MAP at :371-372 and the GO TO COMMON-RETURN at :373 - a forward-only GO TO reproduced as a plain return with its evaluation order and fall-through outcome intact (rule R7), bypassing the trailing IF INPUT-ERROR at :387-392 and reaching :395. Inside 9000-READ-ACCT the three reads are separated by three guards at :696-715, and only the first of them is live. :697-699 tests FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK, which no arm has set - the commented-out IF DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-CARDXREF above it at :696 is preserved as written - so the account read proceeds. :704-706 tests DID-NOT-FIND-ACCT-IN-ACCTDAT, an 88-level that can NEVER be true because the only SET that would raise it is commented out at :792; that is the preserved legacy defect case10 documents, and it is immaterial here only because the account read succeeds. :708 then moves CDEMO-CUST-ID into WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID and :710-711 performs the customer read, which is the site this case drives. The guard after it at :713-715 tests DID-NOT-FIND-CUST-IN-CUSTDAT, equally never true because its SET is commented out at :842, and equally immaterial because 9400 is the last read in the paragraph. The data behind the two successful reads is real. CCXREF holds fixture rows 0-2 of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, whose XREF-ACCT-ID spans - offset 25, length 11 per CVACT03Y - are accounts 00000000050, 00000000027 and 00000000002; the typed ACCTSIDI is 00000000050, so the EXEC CICS READ at :727 against DATASET('CXACAIX ') with an 11-byte RIDFLD and LENGTH(50) finds row 0 and takes WHEN DFHRESP(NORMAL), where :739 moves XREF-CUST-ID 000000050 into CDEMO-CUST-ID and :740 moves XREF-CARD-NUM 0500024453765740 into CDEMO-CARD-NUM. CXACAIX is a PATH over the CCXREF base cluster, reached through the single CardXrefRepository's alternate-key finder and never through a second repository or a second table (gate G45). ACCTDAT holds fixture row 49 of acctdata.txt, which is account 00000000050, so the EXEC CICS READ at :776 against DATASET(LIT-ACCTFILENAME) - the PIC X(8) literal 'ACCTDAT ' of :184-185, trailing space included - with RIDFLD(WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X), KEYLENGTH(11), INTO(ACCOUNT-RECORD) and LENGTH(300) succeeds and :788 SETs FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER. The customer read at :826 against DATASET(LIT-CUSTFILENAME) - 'CUSTDAT ' of :188-189 - with a 9-byte RIDFLD, the PIC X(09) REDEFINES at :76-77 of the id the cross reference supplied, and LENGTH(500), is the one that fails. Its WHEN OTHER body runs in source order: :859 SET INPUT-ERROR TO TRUE, :860 SET FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK TO TRUE, :861 MOVE 'READ' TO ERROR-OPNAME, :862 MOVE LIT-CUSTFILENAME TO ERROR-FILE, :863 MOVE WS-RESP-CD TO ERROR-RESP, :864 MOVE WS-REAS-CD TO ERROR-RESP2, :865 MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG. There is no IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF guard on this arm, unlike the NOTFND arm's :845, and the WS-LONG-MSG alias at :866 and the PERFORM SEND-LONG-TEXT at :867 both stay commented out, as they are in the source (practice B5). The message is the point of this case, and it is arithmetic rather than prose. WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE is declared at :86-105 as nine items: FILLER X(12) 'File Error: ', ERROR-OPNAME X(8), FILLER X(4) ' on ', ERROR-FILE X(9), FILLER X(15) ' returned RESP ', ERROR-RESP X(10), FILLER X(7) ',RESP2 ', ERROR-RESP2 X(10) and a trailing FILLER X(5) of spaces, which re-sums by hand as 12+8+4+9+15+10+7+10+5 = 80 (practice B11). Two of those items are filled here by cross-width moves whose padding is easy to get wrong and is stated rather than assumed: MOVE 'READ' into PIC X(8) gives READ followed by FOUR spaces, and MOVE the PIC X(8) literal 'CUSTDAT ' into PIC X(9) gives CUSTDAT followed by TWO - the seven characters, the literal's own trailing space, and one more gained on the way into the wider receiver. MOVE WS-FILE-ERROR-MESSAGE TO WS-RETURN-MSG then moves 80 characters into the PIC X(75) declared at :117, and a COBOL alphanumeric receiver truncates on the RIGHT, so the last five characters are discarded - and they are exactly the trailing FILLER X(5), five spaces, so nothing but padding is lost, which is why this truncation is safe rather than merely tolerated. :532 moves the surviving 75 bytes into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), re-padding by exactly 3, which is why the expected image measures 78 and ends in four spaces: one from ERROR-RESP2's own PIC X(10) justification and three from the widening. The two response codes are not case data and cannot drift (practice B7). ForcedOutcome.resp and .resp2 are deliberately NOT declared, because the adapter reads only .outcome at :320-322 and a declared code would be inert and therefore misleading; the rendered values are compile-time constants instead. A forced OTHER on the customer site makes readCustomer at :629-631 answer CustomerRepository.ReadResult.of(PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS), a status carrying no CICS response, so AccountViewController.cicsResp falls through FileStatus.cicsRespOfBatchStatus to FileStatus.RESP_NOT_REPORTED = -1, and responseCodeImage renders it through FileStatus.respNotReportedImage as NINE '*' characters left justified in PIC X(10) rather than as a number - so that 'no code was reported' can never be mistaken for the code zero, which is DFHRESP(NORMAL) and would read as success. The reason code has none to report either and renders as nine zeros. That is the difference from case09, whose cross-reference repository does surface a RESP and whose message therefore carries nine digits. The rest of the screen follows from the two flags, and the flag that was NOT set matters as much as the one that was. 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS takes its ELSE at :464 because EIBCALEN is 172, and with FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK false :468 echoes the typed CC-ACCT-ID into ACCTSIDO. FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER satisfies the ordered OR at :471-472, so the ten account items at :473-490 are projected from ACCTDAT row 49: ACSTTUSO Y; the three PIC X(10) dates 2011-04-22, 2023-03-09 and 2023-03-09 from ACCT-OPEN-DATE, from ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE carrying CVACT01Y's own misspelling verbatim, and from ACCT-REISSUE-DATE; ACCT-GROUP-ID as ten spaces; and the five PIC S9(10)V99 amounts through PIC +ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ.99 at width 15 each - +        492.00 from the stored image 00000004920{ whose trailing overpunch is a digit and a sign in one byte, +      6,169.00, +      4,587.00, and +           .00 for both cycle amounts, where the integer positions suppress to spaces and the two decimal digits remain because the mask ends .99 and not .ZZ. FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is never set, so the IF at :493 is skipped and all eighteen customer items stay LOW-VALUES - x'00', not spaces and not an edited zero - which is the proof that the customer read failed rather than returned a blank record, and the hyphenating STRING at :496-504 that replaced the direct MOVE CUST-SSN commented out at :495 never runs. 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS moves DFHBMFSE into ACCTSIDA at :543 and DFHDFCOL into ACCTSIDC at :555, and then declines to change it: the IF FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :557-559 does NOT fire, because this arm set FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK at :860 - the CUSTOMER flag, not the account flag the other two failure paragraphs set - so a customer failure never colours the account number red, and neither does the blank-and-REENTER pair at :561-565 that would add the asterisk. That is gate G38 asserted in its negative form, DFHRED withheld and no '*' anywhere, the counterpart to the positive proof case05 makes; the DFHRED and DFHBMSCA attribute mnemonics themselves come from common.BmsAttributes, reproduced from IBM CICS documentation because DFHBMSCA, DFHAID and DFHATTR are IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D), and the highlight is applied inline at :556-565 because COACTVWC does not copy CSSETATY. The cursor EVALUATE TRUE at :546-552 has three arms whose bodies are identical - FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK, FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK and WHEN OTHER all MOVE -1 TO ACCTSIDL - and they are preserved as three rather than collapsed into one (practice B5), which is why cursorField is ACCTSIDL on every path. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR rather than the DFHBMDAR of :568 because :528-530 flipped WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE, set at :689, to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT before :567 tested it, which is also why INFOMSGO carries the prompt of :113-114 - a literal of exactly 40 characters, counted, which fills WS-INFO-MSG PIC X(40) with no padding of its own and then gains five trailing spaces on the way into INFOMSGO PIC X(45). 1400-SEND-SCREEN moves LIT-THISMAPSET and LIT-THISMAP at :579-580 and SETs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :581, so the reply names COACTVW, CACTVWA and context 1, and the whole conversation - the AID, the commarea and the screen values - travels in the payload with no server-side session state whatsoever (gate G37, rule R6). CDEMO-CUST-ID and CDEMO-CARD-NUM are populated here, unlike in the cross-reference failure cases, because the NORMAL arm at :739-740 ran first. INPUT-ERROR was set at :859 and changes nothing about the exit, because :364 had already been evaluated before 9000-READ-ACCT ran. COACTVWC writes nothing - three keyed reads and no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE anywhere - so expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion rather than an absence of interest, all four seeded rows are pinned unchanged on the final-state channel at their declared widths of 50 and 300 with FILLER present and space-filled (gates G19 and G21), CUSTDAT is pinned at zero rows and 500 bytes because an empty dataset is still a fixed-width one, and expectedReturnCode is 0: an online WHEN OTHER builds a message and paints a screen, and COACTVWC contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' at all - zero occurrences, counted - so gate G35 does not apply and neither an abend nor a non-zero status is asserted anywhere. The unit is reached as a plain Java object, AccountViewController constructed through its four-argument constructor with three fixture-backed repository stubs and a fixed clock, with no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). Nine read outcomes are pinned across three call sites with no two cases overlapping (gate G47): case03 drives all three reads to NORMAL, the 9200 NOTFND at :741 is driven from the harness at :1801-1824 because case08 rejects its input before any read is reached, case09 drives the 9200 WHEN OTHER at :759 on CXACAIX, case10 the 9300 NOTFND at :789 and case11 the 9300 WHEN OTHER at :809 on ACCTDAT, case12 the 9400 NOTFND at :839 - and this file is the only one that pins the 9400 WHEN OTHER arm, so removing or re-pointing it would leave that arm undriven and would additionally duplicate case11. Provenance: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/COACTVWC.cbl, from the 300-byte CVACT01Y, 50-byte CVACT03Y and 500-byte CVCUS01Y layouts including their FILLER spans, from the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COACTVW.CPY, from the CICS file names in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD and from the real app/data/ASCII fixtures - and none of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution, which this environment cannot perform (risk R-A). The images are US-ASCII and never a platform default (practice B8), the clock is pinned at 2022-07-19T23:15:58 so CURDATEO is 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO is 23:15:58, TITLE01O comes from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:19 and TITLE02O from its ACTIVE :22 with :21 commented out - neither of them CCDA-THANK-YOU at :23, which is a different field - and the cross-reference rows are seeded at the fixture's own 36 bytes and padded to the 50 CVACT03Y declares by the declared normalisation, the one fixture in the repository that does not match its copybook (gate G16, risk R-F). review_rules reports that no user rules were provided for this project, so no user rule governs this file; its absence is not licence to lower the bar, and the enterprise practices B1 through B12 bind in their place. WHICH READ IS DRIVEN, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED: the forcedOutcomes member above is keyed by repository operation, and all three of COACTVWC's file verbs are READ - the EXEC CICS READs of CXACAIX at :787, ACCTDAT at :843 and CUSTDAT at :864 - so the key alone cannot say which of them reports the outcome. It used to be INFERRED from whichever dataset this file happened to declare empty, which was a sound rule but a convention: a reader could not see which read was driven without knowing the rule and cross-checking three inputs entries, and no case could drive a read of a dataset that still held rows. unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes now NAMES the site, once, in the same file as the expectation that depends on it. The old rule survives as a required cross-check rather than as the decision: the named site must also be this case's one empty dataset - an empty dataset is one whose rows cannot answer any key, which is exactly why the outcome must be supplied rather than seeded, and because the other two still hold their rows the reads before it still succeed and the flow still reaches the site being driven. Two declarations that disagree are refused rather than one being quietly honoured.
